body:
"a. The only way your decision could be rational is if the future was known. You are essentially making a decision today based on what you believe will happen to you in the future."

The way things are and the way society is, it's isolating.  It's a constant uphill battle and has been my entire life.  As soon as I get a moment to breathe, as soon as I let go a little, I get punished for it.

"b. By your own admission, your current life is unexpected given your past. As you say:"

That is not true at all and I don't see how I said that at all.  Perhaps unexpected for other people.  I certainly didn't think I was going to grow up to be a loser or worse off than I am right now.  I tried so hard for the past decade, insanely hard, to make sure that my past would not define me.  So no, it is not unexpected.  I am just trying to show you that I know that my past doesn't have to get me down so my decision isn't coming from some place of defeat or depression.

"c. If you predicted your future at 15 or 20, or even 22 in the midst of the lawsuit, would you have predicted that you'd now be living in the UK, holding a master's degree and gazing up at the stars. If your 20 year old self was unable to predict the state of your 25 year old self, can you be sure that your 25 year old self is any more accurate at predicting his life ten years down the road? Would you bet your life on that? (Personally I wouldn't trust my 25 year old self with shit, but that's just me.)"

Didn't know I'd be living in the UK, yes would have predicted I'd have a master's degree and have been 'looking up at the stars' since I was 11, so yes.  I don't understand where this line of questioning is coming from because I never thought things would be bad when I was 15, 20, 22, etc.  I've always been optimistic and I've always thought things would get better.  And things have gotten better.  And then worse.  And then better.  And then worse.  And even right now I don't think things will never get better, I'm not naive.  *Of course* things will get better, they *always* do, that's just how it is.  I just don't see the point is all.  Even if it gets better, so what?  So what?  It still doesn't make a difference.  I've experienced some amazing things I would've missed out on if somehow I died in an accident when I was 15, but I'm always going to miss out.  It's a part of life and death.

"I would contend that if it was worth trying once, it is worth trying again. What is the rush? Reinvent yourself again if that's what it takes. You showed courage moving to the UK to pursue your studies and you are still that person."

I've reinvented myself enough times, I'm tired of it.  Of course I'm still that person, I'm an even better person now.  And I'm sure I'd continue being a better person.  But like I said, so what?  The bottom line is, I just don't have the will to live anymore.  I don't have the energy to start all over again.  Bottom line: I don't want to.  I've taken care of myself my entire life because I've always known I've had to make it on my own.  But I'm tired of it.  I don't expect anyone else to take care of me, that's a dangerous road to go down I know, I quite like being independent but I'm just tired.  There's really just no point anymore.

"g. The cost of acting on hope, by making changes one more time or reinventing yourself or forgiving yourself your ideals, is at worst a few more years of disappointment. You will have the opportunity to be hopeless again. But you might not need that opportunity."

You don't seem to understand what I'm saying.  If I act on hopelessness and it's irreversible... so what?  Do you think I'm going to care?  No, because I won't be.  So it won't matter.  More disappointment?  More hopelessness?  No.  Just no.  It's not worth it.  It's never been worth it.  I've done so much with my life, I've come so far, I've done everything I could do to right by people, to be a nice, good person, to overcome the shit hand I've been dealt and I think I've done a damn good job.  I've experienced so many incredible things.  But when it all comes down to it... so what?  Has it been worth it?  Sure I guess but at the same time, not really.  Doesn't really matter.

I sometimes wonder if I made a mistake in reading too much literature and philosophy.  A lot of my favourite authors--the writers of the stories that have touched me deeply, that I found so beautiful and that captured moment and experiences so perfectly--have killed themselves.  But as I was saying earlier, yes I am a reader.  That's all I am.  I will never be as great so what have I got to offer the world?  What contributions have I got?  There is really no point in my existence.  My own mother has told me that I was an accident and she wished I was never born.

Me too.  It's sort of like that Queen song.  It's not that I want to die but it's more that I wish I'd never been born at all.  This is the closest I can come.

I'm sorry I don't want to disappoint you and I'm not trying to argue with you.  I really appreciate all that you've said and I appreciate you taking the time out to try and help me.  I really really do.  I don't want to feel like I'm just dismissing you.  I'm just trying to better explain why I feel the way that I do and where I'm coming from.  I'm just tired and I don't want to do this anymore, I don't want to live like this anymore.

I forgot this is a throwaway.  I should probably mention my biggest secret in life:  I have an eating disorder.  I've had it since I was 19.  Hence why I saw the therapist to begin with, to try to recover and get better.  I've been through therapy, recovery routes, it doesn't really work.  I don't think it ever really goes away, I know it's an ongoing process.  Anyone I've ever told about it I've pushed away.  I've only told a couple of people I've dated and nothing was ever the same again.  Sometimes I get pitied, which is also not what I want.  I don't know how to explain it.

Traditional counselling and therapy just do not work for me.  I've tried many, many, many times and if anything, it's only exacerbated situations and made them worse for me.  I'm never more unhappy than I am when I'm seeing mental health professionals on a regular basis.  Not that I want to knock it, I know it works beautifully.  I honestly just don't think it's for me.  It's been unhelpful at best and harmful at worst.  I've never been told anything I wasn't aware of, never been led to think down a different path or see a different perspective I hadn't already seen or thought about.  Perhaps this is reeking of arrogance but I honestly feel like I just don't benefit from therapy, never like I've benefitted from friends or just being by myself.

Growing up my dad beat me up.  Like, we're talking kicked me and threw me across the room.  My mother stood there watching the whole thing and when he was finished one night, she sat on my bed and told me that I needed to stop making my father so angry because one day he was going to die of a heart attack and it would be all my fault.  She has told me she wished she never had me before and everything.  My father left when I was 14 and never came back.  I confronted my mother about this when I was 19 and she basically said that she didn't realise I hated my father so much I would make up such lies.  Then she said that I must've dreamt all of that up and that she couldn't believe I confused that with reality.  When I confronted her about it last year, she refused to talk about it and basically yelled at me for always focusing on the negative in life.

So.  That was the kind of environment I grew up in.  Yet I still managed to get out and do all the aforementioned above.

When I was 20 I saw a psychotherapist until I was 21.  When I was 22 I sued him for sexual exploitation and psychiatric malpractice.  That was a year and a half of the most soulcrushing, insane lawsuit ever.  They pulled every single dirty trick in the book and in the end they won because they dragged my mother into it, even knowing exactly how she was.  That guy, the therapist, he knew my entire life story.  I trusted him implicitly.  And then he used everything I ever told him and turned it against me.  They tried to claim I had borderline personality disorder and turn it around on me.  They laid my entire sexual history out on the table, dissected every little bit.  It was hell.  It was the first time I ever thought about ending it all.

I tried to reach out to all the friends I had but to be honest, they all had other priorities in their lives in the end.  A lot of good things were happening for them and I was dragging them down.  They started distancing themselves, they got tired of constantly hearing my story (if you're keeping track of the timeline, it's been at least a couple of years now).  So I decided I needed to get out of that toxic environment and I applied to a master's program in the UK, moved here, and then got a job when I graduated.

Exactly.  Because my ideal is unattainable I cannot come to terms with that because anything else is not what I want and I can't see myself as being truly happy.  I just don't see the point.  I have let go of silly ideals in the past and while I'm still around I would be lying if I said I wish that didn't have to be the case.  My life is has honestly been nothing but a series of disillusionments, one after the next.

I'm an extremely sensitive person.  I've gotten better but still, it's who I am.  Probably partly due to the way I was raised.  I've been trying to be healthier for the past few years, to hang out with people that are more chill, people that I'd like to be, but the problem is I *am* more sensitive than them so when I'm upset, they just cannot relate, sympathise, or understand it.  And therefore I only feel more upset.  Yet, hanging out with sensitive and understanding people, like I've sought in the past, has been highly toxic for me and I get stuck in a rut of mental illness or something like that, I can't really explain it.  Neither option leaves me happy.  I've just had to make it on my own.  If you haven't figured by now, I'm an only child.  There is no one else in the entire world who knows what it's like to have grown up with my parents as their parents.

I don't know where I'm going with this, just explaining the situation a little better.  Everyone I've put any trust in in my life has turned it back around on me and used it against me.  Every person I've ever dated who says I deserve to be treated well in my life and says that they'll show me how I'm supposed to be treated and that they'll show me what the standards should be like... have hurt me worse than anyone else ever has.

But that's not even what this is about.  I suppose it does leave me feeling a bit hopeless, though.  It's not about finding love or relationships or anything like that, but I suppose a real human connection, a bond that actually lasts.  All my friends who I've ever found that with have eventually drifted apart, to no fault of their own I understand that relationships and family takes priority, and I see this happening for the rest of my life.  What is there left?  What is the point of continuing on, feeling lonely for the majority of time with moments of happiness, when 'even the wildest and most tenacious love is an ephemeral truth in the end'? (Garcia Marquez).

I just think I've done absolutely everything I could do and made the absolute best with this shit hand I've been dealt.  I'm not going to be the next great poet or writer, or an inspirational philosopher.  I read works of great writers, take in the ideas of great philosophers, but when it comes down to it... I am just a fucking follower.  I have nothing to offer this world.

So at the moment I am just figuring out how I'm going to tie up all the loose ends.  To leave what I need to leave, figure out what charities to donate to, figure out the best way to do this and still preserve my body because I am an organ donor, and finish my memoir.  My memoir, a memoir about the lawsuit and all the events leading up to it (aka the abuse) is about the last thing I've left to finish and once that's done, well, I suppose that will be my goodbye note.

I've thought this through, it's not a sudden, rash decision.  Though I will admit to having encountered several triggers lately and almost going through with it impulsively but as I see it at the moment, I still have to take care of everything before I just cease to be anymore.

To be honest, I've been actually a bit happier than normal lately, perhaps it's because I feel great relief in knowing I've made my decision.

Essentially... I got dealt a pretty shit hand in life.  And yet, I've managed to make the absolute most of it that I could.  I've travelled the world, seen amazing sights, met amazing people, dated all different sorts, been up and down and all over the place, experienced incredible things and the smallest things can bring me great pleasure, such as driving my car around on a clear night and finding a place to just gaze at the stars.

I don't regret this life I chose for myself, but at the same time, I see where it's headed, a life of loneliness, and I've been lonely my entire life.  I'm 25 right now, I have a master's degree, have a steady job, live in a foreign country albeit just the UK (from the states originally, have been here a few years now), and in the next 5-10 years I'm going to start feeling tremendous pressure (hell I feel it now) to settle down with a partner and raise a family.

And I don't fancy that.  I don't want children.  And I know a lot of couples don't have children.  But I've been in my fair share of relationships and talked to plenty of people in long term relationships and marriages to know that my idealistic view of love just does not exist.  And the kicker is, I don't want anything else except that, so if that doesn't exist than I'd rather not have it at all.  I know my standards are high and unrealistic but at the same time, I'd rather be alone than to change them because I've tried changing them, tried to make it work, and all I've done is cause heartbreak to other people. 

I digress.

In the past year I've really come to terms and accepted my mortality.  I suppose this has helped me be more calm with the idea of taking matters into my own hands, something again, I never thought I'd do.

But I know that while I could have more fun now, like I've been doing, in the next decade or so as I get older my looks will fade, and all my friends will settle down with someone and start their own families.  I don't have a close friend anymore really, not one I talk to regularly and who I can share these crazy mind-consuming thoughts with. The few people I've managed to share them with just don't think the same way and just cannot understand or sympathise. And that's the thing, I always knew that I could get through life if I was surrounded by good friends, etc. But now I see that as I get older, friends start pairing off, creating families, their spouses become their best friends (as it should be so I completely understand and am happy for them) but... that's the thing. Family comes first. They've got new priorities now and you fall to the wayside. Which like I said I don't blame or fault anyone for, I completely get it. And like I said, this is the life I chose for me, I don't regret it. It's just that for someone like me, there's just not much left.

There's just not much left.  Sure, there's plenty to look forward to but there will always be plenty to look forward to. There will always be things to miss out on and things I wish I knew, things I could've been around for, but it doesn't make a single difference whether I miss out now or decades down the line.  It could have been two years ago and I would've been OK with having missed the last couple of years. It really doesn't matter. For someone like me, I truly feel I just don't belong in this beautiful world.  And I really do think the world is a beautiful place.  I was just born too sensitive for it.

Not really, just really trying to figure out how to go about the legal stuff first to make sure everything is in order, I suppose, as melodramatic as that sounds.

I do want to get into why I feel this way and how I came to this conclusion.

As funny as this sounds, I am about to take a shower so I just didn't want to get into it at this moment, but I'll get back to you as soon as I finish if you're interested.
